why_those_scans_cannot_pass_here.cause: the slice has one matrix, so it is scanned against itself. Every cross-split scan is therefore comparing a row with a copy of itself, and every one of them is answering a question the slice is not in a position to ask
why_those_scans_cannot_pass_here.where_it_is_asked_for_real: S21D6-030 scans D5's conformal matrix against D6's certification matrix, which are disjoint corpora with disjoint authorship. A red row there is a finding; here it is arithmetic

admission.derivation_reading: split conformal replaces the zero-error prefix: the bar is a quantile of the wrong decisions' margin distribution rather than the position of the single highest-scoring error, so coverage degrades smoothly with alpha instead of being hostage to one point; what it buys costs the zero — the record states an error budget and a bound, never a claimed zero rate. Alpha bounds the leak rate P(admitted | the decision is wrong), not the error rate among admitted decisions: the bar is a quantile of the margins of errors, so a fresh error clears it with probability at most alpha. The second quantity is the one §2.3 cares about, it is roughly the first times the error rate over the coverage, and it is measured on the certification half rather than guaranteed here — errors_admitted counts it and error_upper_bound_95 bounds it. Both readings hold only if the two halves are exchangeable, which is a claim about how the corpus was authored and not something this module can check
admission.derivation_rule: score every independent clean calibration decision with the sealed pairwise-contrastive margin; split the calibration groups into a conformal half and a certification half with no shared fitted vector; take the margins of the answered decisions the ranker got wrong in the conformal half, sort them ascending, and set the threshold to the ceil((1-alpha)*(m+1))-th smallest of the m wrong margins; admit the certification decisions scoring strictly above it; report coverage over independent certification decisions, the errors among admitted decisions, and the Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95% upper bound on the true error rate among admitted decisions

fixture_bar_for_the_artifact_binding.why_none: the conformal half produced 0 wrong margins, so no alpha yields a quantile: with no wrong decision there is no wrong-margin distribution to take one from

admission.margin_floor_admits: nothing; no quantile exists and a component without a bar must abstain
admission.rule: split conformal, S21D6's one change to the map from a ranked group to a decision
admission.split_rule: alternating fold positions, stated before the margins were read; the conformal half places the bar and the certification half is measured against it
admission.why: D6's bar is derived once, at S21D6-034, from the sealed conformal half of 400 outcomes. This one is the fixture's, and it exists to show that admission runs at a derived bar rather than at a constant somebody typed

why_the_pre_registered_alpha_cannot_prod.arithmetic: the conformal half holds 2 decisions, so at most that many wrong margins; it held 0. The finite-sample rank ceil((1-0.20)*(m+1)) is 1, which exceeds them, so the quantile does not exist
why_the_pre_registered_alpha_cannot_prod.this_is_the_rule_working: the module records the rank it computed precisely so a reader can see why no bar exists rather than only that none does. A four-candidate group cannot support a 0.20 bar at any m, which is a fact about the fixture and not a finding about the corpus
why_the_pre_registered_alpha_cannot_prod.what_the_predecessor_did_with_the_same_d: S21D5-024's zero-error prefix rule saw four clean decisions, took the every_answered_decision_was_correct branch, admitted everything and ran the ranking at a floor of zero. The conformal rule admits nothing instead. That difference on identical fixture data is the sprint's change, executed

direction.why_that_is_said_rather_than_hidden: one group cannot both fit and evaluate a direction honestly. The slice proves the wiring -- that a direction is fitted, sealed, stored, reloaded and ranked with -- and D6 fits none at all: S21D6-034 reads the sealed 720 direction
